runs.u: Which project-management tool would you pick?
runs.reply:
It depends on your team’s size, workflow, and tolerance for complexity — but if I had to pick one broadly useful project-management tool, I’d choose **Linear** for software/product teams and **Asana** for general business teams.

### My pick by use case

| Use case | Best pick |
|---|---|
| Software/product development | **Linear** |
| Cross-functional business projects | **Asana** |
| Highly customizable workflows/databases | **Notion** |
| Enterprise-heavy teams | **Jira** |
| Simple visual task tracking | **Trello** |
| All-in-one docs + tasks + wikis | **ClickUp** or **Notion** |
| Client-facing agency work | **Monday.com** |

### If you want one recommendation

**Pick Linear if your team builds software.**  
It’s fast, clean, opinionated, and excellent for issues, cycles/sprints, roadmaps, and GitHub/Slack integrations. It avoids a lot of Jira-style bloat.

**Pick Asana if your team is not primarily engineering-focused.**  
It’s flexible, easy to adopt, good for timelines, owners, dependencies, recurring work, approvals, and cross-team coordination.

### My short answer

If this is for a modern product/engineering team: **Linear**.  
If this is for general company-wide project management: **Asana**.
